'''Mahi R. Singh''' (b. 1949) is a professor of physics at Western University researching [[Nanotechnology|nanoscience]]. He was awarded the Fulbright US-Canada Research Chair for 2021-2022.<ref name=":3">{{cite web|title=Fulbright Canada Alumni Database
|url=https://www.fulbright.ca/alumni/alumni-databases/fulbright-canada-database}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=RECENT CANADIAN FULBRIGHT SCHOLARS in 2021-2022
|url=https://www.fulbright.ca/programs/canadian-scholars/recent-grantees}}</ref>

==Early life==

Singh was born in 1949 in Hamirpur, India.<ref name=":2">{{cite news |date=Jan 16, 2022 |title=BRIEF BIOGRAPHY OF SINGH |publisher=India News Paper:Amar Ujala(Allahabad Edition) |pages=08}}</ref> He received his B.Sc. degree in T.D. College campus; and both M.Sc. (1970) and PhD (1976) degrees from [[Banaras Hindu University]] in condensed matter physics.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Mahi R. Singh biography|url=https://www.hilarispublisher.com/editor/mahi-r-singh-4231}}</ref>

==Academic career==

Singh was awarded Humbold Fellow in [[University of Stuttgart|Stuttgart University]] from 1979 to 1981. Between 1981 and 1985 he was a Research Associate and Lecturer at [[McGill University]]. From 1982 to 1983 he worked in High Magnetic Field Lab, [[Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier University|Université Paul Sabatier]] as a visiting scientist. He also worked as Research Associate at [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]].<ref name=":0" /> 

He joined the [[University of Western Ontario]] as associate professor in 1985. Currently he is professor in this university. He was also a visiting professor at [[Texas Center for Superconductivity]] from June till November in 1992. He also worked as a chief researcher at Superconductors Division of [[Hitachi]], Tokyo between November 1992. During May and August in 2022, he became Fulbright US-Canada Research Chair in [[Vanderbilt University]].<ref name=":3"></ref>

His visiting positions include Texas Center for Superconductivity (1992), [[University of Oxford]] (1993-1994), and Dubna and Ioffe Institute Saint Petersburg (2019).<ref>{{cite web|title=Mahi R. Singh Hilaris SRL |url=https://www.hilarispublisher.com/editor/mahi-r-singh-4231}}</ref>

==Research==
Research topics include:
*[[Nanomaterials]] and [[Nanocomposites]]
*[[Nanophotonics]], [[Plasmonics]], and [[Polaritonics]]
*[[Graphene]] and Carbon [[Nanostructures]]
*Metallic Nanostructures
*Second Harmonic Generation
*[[Photonic]]
*[[Metamaterials]]
*[[Biomaterials]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Research Activities - Mahi R. Singh - Western University (uwo.ca) |url=https://physics.uwo.ca/~msingh/research_interest/index.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mahi R. Singh - Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=UDE5oB8AAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref>
